issues.title: The Future Is Now
issues.dek: Hauss Hejny Headlines a Star-Studded All-American Lineup as College Football’s Best Look to Cement Their Legacies in BLAM History
issues.author: BLAM News
issues.coverAlt: BLAM Magazine cover: Season 4 All-Americans in their team uniforms, with Heisman winner Hauss Hejny holding the trophy in front

blocks.p: The lights are brighter. The expectations are higher. And the talent across the BLAM College Football League has never looked more dangerous.

As Season 4 unfolds, BLAM NEWS proudly unveils its latest magazine cover, celebrating an extraordinary collection of All-American talent representing some of college football’s most competitive programs.

From dominant defensive linemen and lockdown cornerbacks to explosive linebackers and a Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback, this group represents the standard of excellence that every program in BLAM is chasing.
But among these stars, one name commands the spotlight.

blocks.pull: Hauss Hejny. West Virginia. Heisman Trophy winner.
blocks.pull2: And he has the hardware to prove it.

blocks.p: In a league where championship aspirations can disappear with one bad Saturday, West Virginia quarterback Hauss Hejny has accomplished something that separates great players from legends.
He captured college football’s most prestigious individual honor: the Heisman Trophy.
The 84-overall redshirt senior brings a unique dimension to the Mountaineers’ offense with his Pure Runner archetype and Human Joystick ability.
Standing 6 feet tall and weighing 213 pounds, Hejny represents the dynamic rushing quarterback capable of turning a broken play into a highlight-reel moment.
His Heisman victory is more than an individual achievement. It is a statement about the caliber of talent competing in BLAM.
With the trophy now part of his legacy, the question becomes whether Hejny can translate individual greatness into the ultimate team accomplishment.

blocks.box: Can West Virginia turn its Heisman success into a national championship?
blocks.p: That storyline alone makes the Mountaineers one of the most intriguing programs to watch.

blocks.h: Defensive Warfare: The Men Who Control the Trenches

blocks.p: Championships may be celebrated by quarterbacks, but they are often won by the players who make life miserable for them.
And Season 4 features some absolute monsters along the defensive front.
If there is one defender opposing offensive coordinators should circle on their scouting reports, it is Lamar Brown.
At 6-foot-4 and 302 pounds, LSU’s defensive tackle is the highest-rated player featured on this magazine cover.
His Pure Power archetype, combined with Pocket Disruptor, Inside Disruptor, Workhorse, and Hammer abilities, makes him a nightmare along the interior defensive line.
Brown isn’t simply occupying blockers. He is built to destroy offensive game plans.
Maryland brings its own wrecking ball to the conversation.
Derrick Simmons, a 6-foot-3, 312-pound redshirt senior, provides the Terrapins with an imposing presence along the defensive line.
His combination of strength, experience, and disruptive abilities gives Maryland a legitimate defensive centerpiece.
The Florida Gators have a dangerous edge defender in Josh Buechele.
The 6-foot-2, 244-pound junior specializes in speed rushing, with Take Down and Pocket Disruptor among his featured abilities.
Buechele gives Florida the type of pass-rushing threat capable of changing a game with one perfectly timed sack.
Never count Alabama out when discussing defensive talent.
Samu Moala, a 6-foot-4, 255-pound redshirt junior, brings speed and athleticism to the Crimson Tide’s defensive front.
With his Quick Jump ability, Moala has the tools to become a disruptive presence off the edge.

blocks.h: Defensive Dominance: TCU Leads the Charge

blocks.p: While defensive linemen create chaos, linebackers are responsible for controlling it.
And few programs featured on this cover boast a defensive collection quite like TCU.
Amerson is the quarterback of the Horned Frogs’ defense.
The sophomore linebacker combines physicality with defensive awareness, making him an important presence in the middle of the field.
With Robber and Bouncer abilities, Amerson has the potential to influence both passing and rushing situations.
Standing 6-foot-2 and weighing 248 pounds, Dominguez brings an intimidating combination of size and physicality.
His House Call, Knockout, and Bouncer abilities make him a dangerous defensive weapon.
The Rebels have their own rising defensive star.
Carreon is a redshirt freshman who already carries an 84 overall rating, an impressive foundation for a player so early in his collegiate career.
With House Call, Bouncer, Winning Time, and Fan Favorite abilities, his future could be particularly exciting.
If these linebackers continue developing, opposing offenses may have serious problems for seasons to come.

blocks.h: No-Fly Zone: The Secondary Takes Over

blocks.p: The modern college football landscape is built around explosive passing offenses.
But these defensive backs have other plans.
Foreman leads the defensive backfield discussion with an impressive 89 overall rating.
His Robber, Blanket Coverage, and Ballhawk abilities make him a dangerous opponent for quarterbacks who underestimate his coverage skills.
Ohio State continues its tradition of producing talented defensive backs.
Anding brings a Field archetype and a combination of Robber and Knockout abilities that could help the Buckeyes limit explosive passing plays.
Medina gives TCU another talented defensive playmaker.
With his Hybrid archetype and Blow Up ability, he provides additional versatility to an already impressive defensive unit.
Middlebrooks is another player worth watching.
The sophomore safety brings a Coverage Specialist archetype alongside House Call, Instinct, Road Dog, and Team Player abilities.
His presence gives Alabama a promising defensive piece with multiple seasons of potential development ahead.
Beyond the individual stars, this magazine cover tells a much larger story about the BLAM College Football League.
Elite talent is distributed across programs with very different championship expectations.
Florida has a dangerous pass rusher. LSU and Maryland possess powerful interior defenders. Alabama continues to build its defensive identity.
Ole Miss has an emerging linebacker. Ohio State has talent in the secondary. And TCU has assembled an especially impressive collection of defensive playmakers.

blocks.pull: Meanwhile, West Virginia has something every program dreams of producing.

blocks.p: The competition is fierce, the expectations are enormous, and the opportunity to establish a lasting legacy has never been greater.
As the BLAM landscape continues to evolve, several questions deserve attention.

blocks.item: Can Hauss Hejny deliver a national championship to West Virginia?
blocks.p: Winning the Heisman is an extraordinary accomplishment. Winning the national championship would elevate his legacy even further.

blocks.item: Is Lamar Brown the most dominant defensive player in BLAM?
blocks.p: At 96 overall, the LSU defensive tackle stands among the premier talents featured in this All-American showcase.

blocks.item: Does TCU possess the most talented defensive core?
blocks.p: With Kobi Foreman, Joel Amerson, Noriel Dominguez, and Taylor Medina, the Horned Frogs have assembled an impressive group of defensive standouts.

blocks.item: Which underclassman will become the league’s next superstar?
blocks.p: Jawuan Carreon and Tiquan Middlebrooks are among the younger players with opportunities to develop into future household names.
And perhaps the biggest question of all:

blocks.box: Which of these All-Americans will ultimately finish their college careers as national champions?

blocks.h: A New Chapter in BLAM History

blocks.p: Individual awards are earned.
All-American recognition is deserved.
But championships?
As Season 4 unfolds, these athletes will carry the expectations of their teammates, coaches, universities, and fan bases.
Some will become legends.
Others will experience heartbreak.
And a select few may have the opportunity to cement their names permanently in BLAM history.
One thing is certain.
The future isn’t coming. The future is already here.
And these All-Americans are ready to take over.

issues.title: The Road to Miami
issues.dek: 12 Teams. One Championship. No Room for Mistakes.
issues.author: BLAM News

blocks.p: The 2029 College Football Playoff field is officially set, and the road to the national championship in Miami is about to begin.

With four teams earning first-round byes and eight others preparing for postseason battles, the stakes have never been higher. Some programs are chasing redemption, others are looking to complete historic seasons, and one team is looking to prove that its championship run was no fluke.
Let’s break down the bracket.
Four programs have earned a direct ticket to the quarterfinals:
Virginia Tech enters as the No. 2 seed.
After capturing the Big 12 Championship with a 31–21 victory over previously undefeated No. 3 West Virginia, the Hokies have earned a valuable first-round bye.

blocks.pull: The Vick Era is officially entering championship territory.
blocks.pull2: Two more wins separate Virginia Tech from the national championship game.

blocks.p: But the road won’t be easy.
Eight teams will battle for the opportunity to advance.

The Backyard Brawl takes on postseason significance. West Virginia enters with a 12–1 record and the Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback, but the Mountaineers are coming off a painful Big 12 Championship loss to Virginia Tech. Can they regroup and keep their championship hopes alive?
Ohio State gets the home-seed advantage, but Illinois has an opportunity to make a statement. This matchup could be one of the most competitive games of the opening round.
Maryland has put together an impressive 11-win season, but Clemson is no stranger to postseason pressure. The Tigers will have to bring their best to pull off the upset.
Two 10-win programs collide. Florida and Oregon both have the talent to make a deep run, but only one will move forward.

West Virginia’s quarterback took home college football’s most prestigious individual award. Now he faces a different challenge: leading his team through the playoff after suffering a championship defeat.
The Mountaineers have a dangerous offense, and nobody should overlook them.

blocks.h3: The Vick Era Is Within Reach

blocks.p: Virginia Tech sits at No. 2 nationally with an 11–2 record and a first-round bye.
The Hokies already have a Big 12 Championship trophy in their possession. Now they’re chasing something bigger.

blocks.box: The question is simple: Can the Vick Era finish the job?

blocks.h3: Who Can Stop TCU and Alabama?

blocks.p: Both programs enter at 12–1 and have earned top-three seeds. With first-round byes, they’ll have additional time to prepare for their quarterfinal opponents.
Neither team should be taken lightly.
The quarterfinals will narrow the field from eight teams to four. The remaining programs will then battle in the semifinals for a chance to compete for the national championship.
And the final destination?

blocks.pull: One team will leave Miami as national champion.
blocks.pull2: Eleven others will be left wondering what could have been.

blocks.p: Virginia Tech has the talent, the momentum, and the No. 2 seed. The Hokies have already proven they can take down an undefeated top-three opponent on the biggest stage in their conference.
But the postseason is a different animal.

blocks.pull: The Big 12 Championship was a statement.
blocks.pull2: The national championship would be a legacy.

blocks.p: The Vick Era is hunting for something bigger.

Will TCU’s historic scoring dominance translate into postseason success?
Can West Virginia complete an undefeated championship run?
Or could Florida, Auburn, Oregon, Virginia Tech, Ohio State, or Clemson turn the entire playoff picture upside down?

blocks.p: One thing is certain.
And for the coaches of the BLAM League, the time for talking is running out.
Soon, the scoreboard will do all the talking.
This has been BLAM NEWS — Edition 03.
Stay tuned. The road to the throne is just getting started.

issues.title: The Race for the Heisman
issues.dek: Four stars. Three schools. One trophy. Who deserves college football's highest honor?
issues.author: BLAM News
issues.coverAlt: The Heisman Memorial Trophy on display

blocks.p: The championship race isn't the only battle heating up across the BLAM League.
While programs fight for playoff positioning and national championship glory, four of college football's brightest stars are competing for something equally prestigious:
And this year's race has a little bit of everything.

A dual-threat quarterback carrying an undefeated West Virginia program. Two explosive Ole Miss receivers rewriting the conversation around offensive production. And a Georgia running back putting together a season that demands national attention.
With the regular season approaching its conclusion, the question is simple: who has truly been the most outstanding player in college football?
Let's examine the four candidates currently leading the race.
West Virginia's undefeated season has been one of the biggest stories in the BLAM League. And standing at the center of that success is quarterback Hauss Hejny.
Forget the traditional definition of a quarterback. Hejny is an offensive weapon capable of beating opponents through the air or on the ground.
With 1,884 passing yards and an astonishing 1,795 rushing yards, the Mountaineers' signal-caller has accumulated 3,679 yards of total offense through those two categories alone.
His 78% completion percentage and just two interceptions demonstrate that he's doing more than simply relying on his athleticism. He's protecting the football while producing explosive plays.
And his latest performance against Rutgers only strengthened his case.
The Mountaineers remain undefeated at 11–0, and their quarterback currently occupies the top position in the Heisman Watch.
Hejny has the strongest all-around résumé in the current field. His combination of rushing production, passing efficiency, and team success makes him the player everyone else is chasing.
Ole Miss sophomore Danny Podlesny has been terrorizing opposing secondaries throughout the 2029 season.
With 1,802 receiving yards on just 68 catches, Podlesny is averaging an incredible 26.5 yards per reception.
That's not simply moving the chains. That's turning routine passing plays into nightmares for defensive coordinators.

Every time Podlesny touches the football, there's a legitimate possibility that he's taking it to the house. And with 22 receiving touchdowns, he has established himself as one of the most dangerous scoring threats in the league.

blocks.h3: Last game: Florida State 24, Ole Miss 23

blocks.p: Despite the narrow defeat, Podlesny remains second in the Heisman Watch.
But there's another interesting storyline developing in Oxford. He's not the only Ole Miss receiver competing for the trophy.

Podlesny might be the most explosive offensive player in the field. His touchdown production is difficult to ignore, and if the award were decided strictly by scoring impact, he'd have a powerful argument.
Georgia's Jerrick Gibson has been putting in WORK.
While the quarterbacks and wide receivers dominate much of the Heisman conversation, Gibson has built his candidacy through consistent production on the ground.

The Bulldogs' senior running back has rushed for 1,535 yards and 16 touchdowns while averaging approximately 9.0 yards per carry. That's an incredible level of efficiency for a player with 171 rushing attempts.
But Gibson isn't limited to running between the tackles. His 33 receptions and 333 receiving yards bring his total production to 1,868 yards from scrimmage.
And at 94 overall, Gibson is the highest-rated player among the four current Heisman candidates.
While he didn't deliver his most explosive performance, his contributions helped the Bulldogs secure another victory.

Gibson has a legitimate argument as the most complete traditional running back in the race. His combination of rushing efficiency, receiving ability, and touchdown production makes him a serious contender.
Imagine being a defensive coordinator preparing to face Ole Miss. You spend the entire week developing a game plan to contain Danny Podlesny.
And then you remember Caleb Cunningham is lining up on the opposite side. Good luck with that.

Cunningham has assembled an outstanding senior campaign, recording 70 receptions for 1,637 yards and 14 touchdowns. He's averaging approximately 23.4 yards per reception, making him another dangerous deep-ball threat in the Rebels' offense.

And while his teammate Podlesny currently sits ahead of him in the Heisman standings, Cunningham has an argument of his own. With a 91 overall rating, he brings elite talent and consistent production to an Ole Miss offense featuring two of the nation's most dangerous receivers.

Cunningham might be overshadowed by his own teammate, but his numbers would make him a headline attraction at almost any other program. The biggest question might be whether having two Heisman candidates helps Ole Miss or divides the spotlight between them.

blocks.h: By the Numbers: The Heisman Showdown

blocks.p: West Virginia's quarterback has been producing at an extraordinary level as both a passer and runner.
Twenty-two receiving touchdowns on 68 catches means approximately one out of every three receptions has resulted in six points.

blocks.item: Ole Miss has TWO Heisman candidates
blocks.p: Podlesny and Cunningham have combined for 138 receptions, 3,439 receiving yards and 36 receiving touchdowns. Those are astonishing numbers for two players sharing the same offense.
With the regular season nearing its conclusion, BLAM News sees a compelling argument for each of the four candidates.
But if the Heisman Trophy were awarded today, based on the available statistics and current standings, our editorial selection would be:
The Mountaineers' undefeated record, combined with Hejny's dual-threat production and exceptional passing efficiency, gives him the strongest overall case.

However, this race is far from settled. Podlesny's touchdown numbers could make him impossible to ignore. Gibson has the production to challenge the leaders. And Cunningham remains one explosive performance away from changing the conversation.
Four candidates. Three programs. One trophy. Only one will be remembered as the 2029 Heisman winner.

blocks.h: BLAM League — We Want to Hear From You!

blocks.p: Coaches, it's time to settle the debate. Who deserves the 2029 Heisman Trophy?
Is the Heisman about individual statistics? Is it about carrying your team to an undefeated season? Or should the most explosive player in college football take home the hardware?
Let the debate begin. This has been another edition of BLAM News.

issues.title: The Hot Seat & Playoff Watch
issues.dek: The playoff picture is taking shape. The coaching carousel is heating up. And for some BLAM League coaches, the pressure is officially on.
issues.author: PKSHADOWMAN
issues.coverAlt: BLAM News Issue #001 cover: The Vick Era, the Hot Seat, and the 2029 playoff bracket

blocks.p: Welcome to the first edition of BLAM News, where we cover the biggest storylines, league developments, coaching drama, and everything happening across the BLAM League.
As the 2029 season approaches its postseason, two major questions are beginning to emerge:

blocks.pull: Who's going to survive the coaching carousel,
blocks.pull2: and who's going to survive the playoff race?

blocks.p: Let's get into it.
The latest National coaching job-security report has revealed some concerning numbers. Twelve head coaches currently appear on the job-security watchlist, with several sitting below 30%.
Here are the coaches currently facing the most pressure:
At just 13% job security, Drinkwitz currently sits at the bottom of the report. Despite a career record of 73–63, the pressure in College Station is clearly worth watching.
Brohm has accumulated 111 career wins, but his current job-security reading is only 18%. That's a concerning position for a coach with that much experience.
With a 16–30 career record and a 23% job-security reading, Iowa's situation deserves attention as the season winds down.
Texas currently sits at 28%. With a 27–24 career record, the question is whether the program can turn things around before the offseason.
Louisville rounds out the five lowest readings. Johnson currently has a 13–32 career record, making this one of the more interesting situations to monitor.
NC State, Arizona State, Utah, Michigan, Boston College, Arizona, and North Carolina also appear on the report.
Their job-security readings range from 37% to 44%. While these numbers aren't as low as the five programs above, they're worth monitoring as the season approaches its conclusion.

The offseason could bring some serious changes to the coaching landscape. Whether these coaches can turn things around remains to be seen. One thing is certain: nobody wants to be looking for a new job when the season ends.

blocks.note: These are in-game job-security readings, not confirmed firings.

blocks.p: Now let's talk football.
The 2029 playoff bracket is beginning to take shape, and the competition for a national championship is getting serious.
With four teams receiving first-round byes, eight others will have to fight their way through the opening round.

One of the most interesting first-round matchups on the board. Penn State and Virginia Tech are both looking to extend their seasons, but only one can advance. The Hokies enter at 8–2, and the Vick Era has put Virginia Tech in position to compete for a championship.
A postseason rivalry matchup with plenty of potential drama. West Virginia enters undefeated at 10–0, while Pittsburgh comes in at 8–2. The question is whether Pitt can disrupt an undefeated season.
Two programs with 8–2 and 7–3 records, respectively. Both have an opportunity to make a statement, but the margin for error is gone.
Indiana has an opportunity to make some noise against Oregon. With both teams entering the bracket, this matchup could have significant implications for the next round.

blocks.h: The Vick Era: Virginia Tech in the Playoff Picture

blocks.p: Let's give the Hokies some attention.
Virginia Tech currently sits at the No. 8 seed with an 8–2 record.
The road ahead won't be easy. Penn State is waiting in the first round, and a win would move the Hokies one step closer to a potential quarterfinal matchup.
The Vick Era has put Virginia Tech in the conversation. Now it's time to see how far the Hokies can take it.
The 2029 season is approaching its most important stretch.
Some programs are preparing for a championship run. Others are fighting to keep their coaches employed. And somewhere in the middle, the coaching carousel is waiting to make its next move.
Will the undefeated teams maintain their momentum? Will a lower seed pull off an upset? And which coaches will still be standing when the offseason arrives?
The playoff race is heating up. The hot seats are getting hotter. And in the BLAM League, the offseason might be just as entertaining as the games themselves.
This has been your first edition of BLAM NEWS.
Stay tuned. We're just getting started.
